questions.stemHtml: Among 100 students, x1 have birthdays in January, x2 have birthday in February, and so on. If x0 = max (x1, x2, …, x12), then the smallest possible value of x0 is
questions.solutionHtml:
12 months share 100 birthdays. If every month had at most 8, the total would be at most 96 < 100, so some month has at least 9: x0 ≥ ⌈100/12⌉ = 9.

9 is achievable: eight months with 8 and four months with 9 give 64 + 36 = 100. Smallest x0 = 9.

questions.stemHtml: A gentleman decided to treat a few children in the following manner. He gives half of his total stock of toffees and one extra to the first child, and then the half of the remaining stock along with one extra to the second and continues giving away in this fashion. His total stock exhausts after he takes care of 5 children. How many toffees were there in his stock initially?
questions.solutionHtml:
Work backwards. If he has S before a child, he is left with S − (S/2 + 1) = S/2 − 1. So S = 2(left + 1).

After the 5th child 0 is left → before the 5th: 2. Then before the 4th: 6, 3rd: 14, 2nd: 30, 1st: 62.

questions.stemHtml: Veeru invested Rs 10000 at 5% simple annual interest, and exactly after two years, Joy invested Rs 8000 at 10% simple annual interest. How many years after Veeru’s investment, will their balances, i.e., principal plus accumulated interest, be equal?
questions.solutionHtml:
Let t be the years after Veeru's investment. Veeru: 10000 + 500t. Joy (invested for t − 2 years): 8000 + 800(t − 2) = 6400 + 800t.

10000 + 500t = 6400 + 800t → 300t = 3600 → t = 12.

questions.stemHtml: If y is a negative number such that 2y2 log35 = 5log23, then y equals
questions.solutionHtml:
Take log base 2: y2 log35 = log23 × log25.

Since log35 = log25 / log23, this gives y2 (log25 / log23) = log23 × log25, so y2 = (log23)2.

y is negative, so y = −log23 = log2(1/3).

questions.stemHtml: Leaving home at the same time, Amal reaches office at 10:15 am if he travels at 8 km/hr, and at 9:40 am if he travels at 15 km/hr. Leaving home at 9:10, at what speed, in km/hr, must he travel so as to reach office exactly at 10 am?
questions.solutionHtml:
Same distance d, times differ by 35 min: d/8 − d/15 = 35/60 → d × 7/120 = 7/12 → d = 10 km.

Leaving at 9:10 to arrive at 10:00 gives 50 min = 5/6 h, so speed = 10 ÷ 5/6 = 12 km/h.

questions.stemHtml: A train travelled at one-thirds of its usual speed, and hence reached the destination 30 minutes after the scheduled time. On its return journey, the train initially travelled at its usual speed for 5 minutes but then stopped for 4 minutes for an emergency. The percentage by which the train must now increase its usual speed so as to reach the destination at the scheduled time, is nearest to
questions.solutionHtml:
At 1/3 speed the time is 3T, so 3T − T = 30 → usual time T = 15 min.

Return: 5 min at usual speed covers 1/3 of the distance, then a 4-min stop. 9 min are gone, 6 min remain for the other 2/3, which normally takes 10 min.

New speed / usual speed = 10/6 = 5/3, an increase of 66.7%, nearest 67.

questions.stemHtml: The number of real-valued solutions of the equation 2x + 2−x = 2 − (x − 2)2 is
questions.solutionHtml:
Compare ranges. By AM ≥ GM, 2x + 2−x ≥ 2, with equality only at x = 0.

The right side 2 − (x − 2)2 ≤ 2, with equality only at x = 2.

Both sides would need to equal 2 at the same x, which cannot happen. Number of solutions = 0.

questions.stemHtml: A solution, of volume 40 litres, has dye and water in the proportion 2 : 3. Water is added to the solution to change this proportion to 2 : 5. If one-fourths of this diluted solution is taken out, how many litres of dye must be added to the remaining solution to bring the proportion back to 2 : 3?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dye 16 L, water 24 L. For 2 : 5 the water becomes 40 L (dye fixed at 16), total 56 L.

Remove 1/4: dye 12 L, water 30 L. For 2 : 3 we need dye = 30 × 2/3 = 20 L, so add 8 litres.

questions.stemHtml: Let A, B and C be three positive integers such that the sum of A and the mean of B and C is 5. In addition, the sum of B and the mean of A and C is 7. Then the sum of A and B is
questions.solutionHtml:
2A + B + C = 10 and A + 2B + C = 14. Subtract: B − A = 4.

Try A = 1, B = 5: 2 + 5 + C = 10 → C = 3 ✓. A = 2, B = 6 gives C = 0, which is not positive. So A + B = 6.

questions.stemHtml: How many 3-digit numbers are there, for which the product of their digits is more than 2 but less than 7?

A straight road connects points A and B. Car 1 travels from A to B and Car 2 travels from B to A, both leaving at the same time. After meeting each other, they take 45 minutes and 20 minutes, respectively, to complete their journeys. If Car 1 travels at the speed of 60 km/hr, then the speed of Car 2, in km/hr, is
questions.solutionHtml:
Meeting-point rule: v1/v2 = √(t2/t1), where t1, t2 are the times taken after meeting.

v2/60 = √(45/20) = 3/2 → v2 = 90 km/h.

questions.stemHtml: If log45 = (log4y)(log6√5), then y equals
questions.solutionHtml:
Write everything with natural logs: ln5/ln4 = (ln y/ln4) × (½ ln5 / ln6).

Cancel ln5/ln4: 1 = ln y / (2 ln6) → ln y = ln36 → y = 36.

questions.stemHtml: A solid right circular cone of height 27 cm is cut into pieces along a plane parallel to its base at a height of 18 cm from the base. If the difference in volume of the two pieces is 225 cc, the volume, in cc, of the original cone is
questions.solutionHtml:
The cut is 18 cm above the base, so the small top cone has height 9 = 1/3 of 27, and volume V/27. The frustum has 26V/27.

Difference = 25V/27 = 225 → V = 243 cc.

questions.stemHtml: Two persons are walking beside a railway track at respective speeds of 2 and 4 km per hour in the same direction. A train came from behind them and crossed them in 90 and 100 seconds, respectively. The time, in seconds, taken by the train to cross an electric post is nearest to
questions.solutionHtml:
Let the train speed be v km/h and its length L. Relative speeds are v − 2 and v − 4: L = (v − 2) × 90 = (v − 4) × 100 (in km/h × s).

90v − 180 = 100v − 400 → v = 22 km/h. L = 20 × 90/3600 = 0.5 km.

Time to pass a post = 0.5/22 h = 1800/22 ≈ 81.8 s → 82.

questions.stemHtml: A circle is inscribed in a rhombus with diagonals 12 cm and 16 cm. The ratio of the area of circle to the area of rhombus is
questions.solutionHtml:
Half-diagonals 6 and 8 give side 10 and area ½ × 12 × 16 = 96.

Inradius = altitude of the right triangle from the centre to a side = 6 × 8 / 10 = 4.8.

Ratio = π(4.8)2/96 = 23.04π/96 = 6π/25.

questions.stemHtml: If f(5 + x) = f(5- x) for every real x, and f(x) = 0 has four distinct real roots, then the sum of these roots is
questions.solutionHtml:
f(5 + x) = f(5 − x) means the graph is symmetric about x = 5, so roots come in pairs r and 10 − r, each pair summing to 10.

If 5 were a root, the other three roots would have to pair up, which is impossible; so the four distinct roots form two such pairs, and their sum = 20.

questions.stemHtml: If x = (4096)7 + 4√3, then which of the following equals 64?

On a rectangular metal sheet of area 135 sq in, a circle is painted such that the circle touches two opposite sides. If the area of the sheet left unpainted is two-thirds of the painted area then the perimeter of the rectangle in inches is
questions.solutionHtml:
Unpainted = 2/3 of painted, so painted = 3/5 of 135 = 81 = πr2 → r = 9/√π.

The circle touches two opposite sides, so the shorter side = 2r = 18/√π and the other side = 135 ÷ (18/√π) = 7.5√π.

Perimeter = 2(18/√π + 7.5√π) = 15√π + 36/√π = 3√π(5 + 12/π).

questions.stemHtml: The number of distinct real roots of the equation (x + 1/x)2 − 3(x + 1/x) + 2 = 0 equals
questions.solutionHtml:
Put t = x + 1/x: t2 − 3t + 2 = 0 → t = 1 or 2.

For real x, |x + 1/x| ≥ 2, so t = 1 is impossible. t = 2 → x2 − 2x + 1 = 0 → x = 1.

Distinct real roots: 1.

questions.stemHtml: If a, b and c are positive integers such that ab = 432, bc = 96 and c < 9, then the smallest possible value of a + b + c is
questions.solutionHtml:
c must divide 96 and be < 9: c ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8}, b = 96/c, and b must divide 432.

c = 8: b = 12, a = 36 → 56. c = 6: b = 16, a = 27 → 49. c = 4: b = 24, a = 18 → 46. c = 3: b = 32, 432/32 not an integer. c = 2: b = 48, a = 9 → 59. c = 1: b = 96, 432/96 not an integer.

Smallest sum = 46.

questions.stemHtml: The area of the region satisfying the inequalities |x| - y ≤ 1, y ≥ 0 and y ≤ 1 is (in numerical value)
questions.solutionHtml:
|x| − y ≤ 1 means |x| ≤ 1 + y. For each y from 0 to 1, x runs from −(1 + y) to 1 + y, a width of 2(1 + y).

The region is a trapezium with parallel sides 2 (at y = 0) and 4 (at y = 1) and height 1: area = ½ × (2 + 4) × 1 = 3.

questions.stemHtml: In a group of people, 28% of the members are young while the rest are old. If 65% of the members are literates, and 25% of the literates are young, then the percentage of old people among the illiterates is nearest to
questions.solutionHtml:
Take 100 people: young 28, old 72. Literates 65, of whom young = 16.25, old = 48.75.

Illiterates = 35; old illiterates = 72 − 48.75 = 23.25. Percentage = 23.25/35 ≈ 66.4%, nearest 66.

questions.stemHtml: The mean of all 4-digit even natural numbers of the form ‘aabb’, where a > 0, is
questions.solutionHtml:
aabb = 1100a + 11b, with a = 1…9 and b ∈ {0, 2, 4, 6, 8} (even), every pair allowed.

Mean = 1100 × mean(a) + 11 × mean(b) = 1100 × 5 + 11 × 4 = 5544.

questions.stemHtml: An alloy is prepared by mixing three metals A, B and C in the proportion 3 : 4 : 7 by volume. Weights of the same volume of the metals A, B and C are in the ratio 5 : 2 : 6. In 130 kg of the alloy, the weight, in kg, of the metal C is
questions.solutionHtml:
Weight ∝ volume × density: A : B : C = 3×5 : 4×2 : 7×6 = 15 : 8 : 42 (total 65).

C = 42/65 × 130 = 84 kg.

questions.stemHtml: A person spent Rs 50000 to purchase a desktop computer and a laptop computer. He sold the desktop at 20% profit and the laptop at 10% loss. If overall he made a 2% profit then the purchase price, in rupees, of the desktop is
How many distinct positive integer-valued solutions exist to the equation (x2 − 7x + 11)(x2 − 13x + 42) = 1?
questions.solutionHtml:
ab = 1 when (i) a = 1, (ii) a = −1 with b even, or (iii) b = 0 with a ≠ 0.

(i) x2 − 7x + 11 = 1 → x = 2, 5.

(ii) x2 − 7x + 11 = −1 → x = 3, 4; the exponents are 12 and 6, both even ✓.

(iii) x2 − 13x + 42 = 0 → x = 6, 7; the bases are 5 and 11, both non-zero ✓.

Total 6 solutions.
